title: SLO Escape Hatch & Priority Loss Prevention — per-endpoint/model SLI taxonomy, error budget escrow, and staged circuit-breaker policy
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Overview:
This ticket defines a pragmatic SLO/SLI taxonomy for per-endpoint and per-model contracts, an error-budget escrow mechanism for graceful capacity borrowing, and an 'escape hatch' policy (staged circuit-breakers + prioritized load shedding) to prevent cascading outages across regions. The goals are to: 1) make SLI computation unambiguous for low-latency and high-throughput routes; 2) allow controlled borrowing of error budget between pinned model variants for short windows; 3) provide an escape hatch orchestration that degrades predictably with tenant-aware priority bands rather than blunt failure.

Background / Motivation:
We have repeatedly observed high bursts (notably during model rollouts and cross-region network partitions) where blunt circuit breakers eject too much capacity or route all traffic to a single variant, causing quality regressions and customer incident escalations. Existing docs (see ENG-31209) define SLO declarations but do not cover escrowed error budget, cross-variant borrowing, nor the staged escape-hatch behavior we need for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Proposed artifacts in this ticket:
- Canonical SLI definitions for three endpoint classes: interactive-chat (latency p95/p99 + quality guardrails), streaming-inference (time-to-first-token + error rate), and batch-embed (throughput + job success rate).
- Error Budget Escrow spec: time-windowed escrow accounts, max borrow fraction per variant, manual vs automatic repayment rules.
- Staged Escape Hatch Orchestration: soft-threshold throttles -> variant demotion -> regional soft-ejection -> hard circuit-breaker.
- Priority Loss Prevention: tenant priority bands, per-tenant graceful eviction matrix, and pinned-variant protection rules.
- Observability and Alerts: telemetry fields to expose in Console and runbooks for ops.

SLI taxonomy (summary):
- interactive-chat endpoints:
  * Availability SLI: successful token stream start within 500ms for p95, within 1s for p99 (success = response begins and no HTTP 5xx).
  * Latency SLI: p95 end-to-end latency for full generation <= configured route threshold.
  * Quality SLI: model answer non-abstain rate on canonical promptset (daily sampling, target >= 98% pass).
- streaming-inference endpoints:
  * TTF (time-to-first-token) p95 <= 120ms; p99 <= 300ms.
  * Continuity SLI: stream not cut mid-response (failure rate <= 0.5% per 1000 requests).
- batch-embed endpoints:
  * Throughput SLI: jobs completed per hour relative to provisioned capacity (>= 99%).
  * Job success SLI: end-to-end success ratio >= 99.5%.

Error Budget Escrow (mechanics):
- Each route variant has an error_budget account (EBA) based on declared SLO and burn rate.
- Escrow window: 1 hour default (configurable), with max borrow fraction = 20% of EBA.
- Borrowing triggers: pre-configured anisotropic signals (burn-rate > 2x AND capacity pressure > 60%).
- Repayment: either automatic (when burn_rate returns < 1x for 2 consecutive windows) or manual via runbook.
- Ledger and audit: every borrow/repay is an event recorded in audit log + Console timeline.

Staged Escape Hatch Policy (decision matrix):
1) Soft throttle: per-tenant token rate capped to preserve p95 for high-priority tenants (applies when route burn-rate between 1.5x-2.5x).
2) Variant demotion: lower-quality-compatible variant used for best-effort traffic (applies when borrow > 10% or regional CPU/GPU saturation > 75%).
3) Regional soft-ejection: shift best-effort traffic to secondary region (applies when regional P95 tail > 2500ms and queue depth > 80th percentile).
4) Hard circuit-breaker: reject low-priority traffic (applies when borrow > 20% or sustained hardware failure).

Priority Loss Prevention rules:
- Priority bands: Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze. Bands map to protected percent of capacity and eviction order.
- Protected frontage: Platinum gets 40% of a route's preserved slice during soft-throttle; Gold 25%; Silver 20%; Bronze 15%.
- Tenant pin rule: Tenants with pinned-variant=true cannot be evicted without manual approval; can still be rate-limited but not demoted.

Multi-region failover integration:
- Failover is driven by regional SLI signatures (latency, error rate, queue growth) and an arbitration policy that prefers gradual evacuation (traffic-weight migration in 5% steps every 30s) rather than instantaneous cutover.
- When error budget escrow is exhausted for a primary region, the orchestration will attempt cross-region borrow with a safety multiplier (max cross-region borrow = 10% unless approved).

Operational observability and alerts:
- Add new telemetry tags: slo.contract_id, slo.window, eskrow.borrow_id, variant.demoted, region.ejection_phase.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO heatmap, escrow ledger view, active escape-hatches timeline.
- Alerts: burn-rate > 2x (P1), escrow borrow initiated (P2), variant demotion (P2), partial region ejection (P0).

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec approved by Reliability and Product (signoffs captured in comments).
- Implementation plan with API changes (route manifest fields for escrow & priority bands).
- Console dashboard mocks reviewed by Design.
- End-to-end e2e test coverage for borrow/repay, staged ejection flows in the chaos harness.

Open questions / risks:
- Multi-tenant fairness: edge cases where many small tenants in Bronze collectively exceed their bands. Proposal: proactive micro-throttles per tenant to prevent collective overruns.
- Billing implications: borrowed capacity and resulting token usage accounting needs finance input (action: @Lena Cho).
- KMS/Audit: escrow ledger must be tamper-evident in Private deployments. Security review flagged that ledger writes require HSM-backed signing for on-prem.
